Jerry Rice: Played college football at Mississippi Valley State.
Was selected 16th overall in the 1985 NFL draft.
Finished his NFL career with 22,895 receiving yards.

Recorded 23 touchdown receptions during the 2007 season.

Lay's Classic: Its ingredient list includes potatoes and vegetable oil.
Its chips have a thin, flat shape without ridges.
The standard American package is predominantly yellow.
Ruffles Cheddar & Sour Cream: Its manufacturer is part of Frito-Lay.

The chips have an orange coating and pronounced waves.
Pringles Original: The product was introduced in the United States in 1968.
Each piece has a uniform saddle-like shape.
The pieces are designed to stack neatly.
Its red cylindrical container features a mustached mascot.

Jimi Hendrix: Served in the United States Army before achieving musical fame.
Frequently played a right-handed guitar restrung for left-handed use.
Performed the American national anthem at Woodstock in 1969.
Eddie Van Halen: Formed a band with his brother Alex.
Frequently used a two-handed tapping technique.
Recorded the instrumental guitar showcase Eruption.
Eric Clapton: Was born in Surrey, England, in 1945.
Was a member of the Yardbirds.
Played guitar in the rock trio Cream.
Recorded the songs Layla and Tears in Heaven.

Toyota: The company was established in Japan in 1937.
Its industrial roots involve automatic weaving looms.
Introduced the Prius in Japan in 1997.
Its passenger car lineup includes the Camry and Corolla.
Honda: The company was established in Japan in 1948.
Motorcycles were central to its early business.
Its passenger vehicles include the Odyssey and Pilot.
The Civic and Accord are two of its longest-running car models.
Porsche: The company began as an engineering consultancy in 1931.
Its headquarters are in Stuttgart, Germany.
Its vehicle lineup includes the Cayenne and Taycan.
Its best-known sports car carries the model number 911.

Ribeye: It contains the longissimus dorsi muscle.
It often features substantial intramuscular fat.
It can be purchased with or without a bone.
It is cut from the same section used for prime rib.
Filet Mignon: It comes from a muscle that performs relatively little work.
It is generally lean with relatively little marbling.
It is cut from the beef tenderloin.
Its name is French and it is commonly served as a thick medallion.
New York Strip: It is cut from the short loin.
It is also commonly called a Kansas City steak.
Its boneless form is traditionally served at American steakhouses.

Breaking Bad: The series originally aired on AMC.
Much of the story takes place in Albuquerque, New Mexico.
Bryan Cranston portrays chemistry teacher Walter White.
The Sopranos: Much of the story takes place in New Jersey.
James Gandolfini portrays a mob boss who attends therapy.
Game of Thrones: It ran for eight seasons on HBO.
It is based on novels written by George R. R. Martin.
The fictional continents include Westeros and Essos.

Michael Phelps: Made his Olympic debut at age 15.
Won eight gold medals at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.
Finished his swimming career with 23 Olympic gold medals.
Usain Bolt: Stands approximately six feet five inches tall.
Won eight Olympic gold medals in sprint events.
Set a 100-meter world record of 9.58 seconds in 2009.
Simone Biles: Was born in Columbus, Ohio, in 1997.
Trained in gymnastics in the Houston area.

Performed a Yurchenko double pike vault in international competition.

Bacon: Traditional preparation involves curing meat with salt.
It can also undergo a smoking process.
American versions commonly come from pork belly.
It is frequently fried in thin strips until crisp.
Pancakes: Versions of this dish exist in many countries.

The batter is poured onto a hot griddle and flipped.
They are commonly served in stacks with butter and maple syrup.
Breakfast Burrito: Modern American versions are associated with New Mexican cuisine.
Common fillings include potatoes and cheese.

The ingredients are wrapped together inside a flour tortilla.

Arnold Schwarzenegger: Won the Mr. Olympia bodybuilding title seven times.
Portrayed a cyborg in the 1984 film The Terminator.
Jackie Chan: Was born in Hong Kong in 1954.
Trained at the China Drama Academy.
Starred in the 1978 martial arts film Drunken Master.
Co-starred with Chris Tucker in the Rush Hour franchise.
Tom Cruise: Was born in Syracuse, New York, in 1962.
Starred in the 1983 film Risky Business.
Portrayed a naval aviator nicknamed Maverick.
Plays Ethan Hunt in the Mission: Impossible franchise.

Tiger Woods: Was born in Cypress, California, in 1975.

Completed a major championship comeback at Augusta in 2019.
Jack Nicklaus: Was born in Columbus, Ohio, in 1940.
Won the U.S. Amateur championship twice.

Arnold Palmer: Was born in Latrobe, Pennsylvania, in 1929.
Served in the United States Coast Guard.

Chocolate Chip: Its modern American recipe originated during the 1930s.

Oreo: The original product was introduced in 1912.
It was first manufactured by the National Biscuit Company.

A white filling sits between two dark round biscuits.
Snickerdoodle: American recipes for this treat date back to the nineteenth century.

A coating of cinnamon and granulated sweetener gives it a speckled finish.

The Simpsons: The characters debuted in short television segments in 1987.
The fictional setting is a town called Springfield.
The central household includes Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa and Maggie.
SpongeBob SquarePants: The series premiered on Nickelodeon in 1999.
Its creator, Stephen Hillenburg, studied marine biology.

Looney Tunes: The original animated shorts began appearing in 1930.
Warner Bros. produced the original series of theatrical cartoons.
Voice actor Mel Blanc portrayed numerous recurring characters.
Its recurring characters include Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck.
